memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'These, then, are the regulations for the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, the guilt offering, the ordination offering and the fellowship offering,'" - Lev 7:37 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the summary. Six offerings, listed together, closing the first great section of Leviticus.

Look at the range of human experience they cover. The burnt offering: total surrender. The grain offering: thanksgiving for provision. The sin offering: cleansing for guilt. The guilt offering: repair for damage done. The ordination offering: setting apart for service. The fellowship offering: celebration and shared joy.

Surrender, gratitude, guilt, restitution, calling, celebration. God provided a way to bring every one of these to Him.

That is the pastoral genius of this system. Israel was never left with an experience that had no home in worship. Whatever a person was carrying — shame, joy, obligation, thankfulness — there was a way to bring it.

Christians sometimes feel they may only bring certain things to God. Praise, yes. Requests, yes. But confusion, anger, grief, guilt, sheer delight? We hesitate.

The Psalms alone should settle this. They contain praise, complaint, terror, joy, rage, and repentance — all addressed to God. Cast all your anxiety on him because he cares for you (1 Pet 5:7).

Every offering finds its fulfilment in Christ. And through Him, there is nothing in your life that cannot be brought to God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there something I have never felt able to bring to God?
2. Which of these six kinds of offering best describes where I am today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that there is nothing in my life that has no place before You. I bring You today exactly what I am carrying. Amen.
